checks.name: stale-names
checks.question: Which symbol-like names in comments are defined nowhere? Names count as defined if they are in any image's ELF symbol table, are a label, .set, .equ, NAME= or .macro anywhere in the tree (archive/ and cruft excluded), or are an identifier in any .c/.h code. A token counts as symbol-like if it has an underscore and an upper-case letter, or is CamelCase with at least 2 humps, and is at least 6 characters long. Elided tokens ('..._CC3_TableLookup', '_Foo', 'Foo_...', 'Foo_*', 'Foo_{A,B}', 'Foo_NN') are matched as a suffix, prefix, infix or wildcard. Each hit also says whether the name is on the OLD side of scripts/renaming/*.sed, *.map or (marked '(py)') the .py dicts, and gives the NEW name and whether it is defined.

checks.name: unread-claims
checks.question: Is anything actually reading what a header says nothing reads? The claims checked are 'no reader found', 'No reader', 'unreferenced', 'no code reference', 'nothing reads it', 'no registration or code reference', NoRef_/Unref_ label names, and bare 'purpose not established' headers that list no readers. The range used is the next label up to the next non-child ELF symbol, unless the claim's own sentence or line states a range or one other address. Signals counted, over the image and its bus peers: ptr32 (an LE24 pointer with a 0 high byte, including SELF hits from inside the blob), pushw hi/lo pairs, srcref (code uses of any symbol in the range, including C NAKA_ADDR/& uses; declarations, aliases and internal branches are excluded), numeric immediates, and ld xiy|xhl,X / ld bc,N / ldir[w] copies overlapping the range. ROM-pointer signals are switched off for images linked below 0x100000 (v142, prom_d).

checks.name: table-counts
checks.question: Does a stated count ('table of N pointers', 'N handler pointers', 'N x u32', 'N entries', 'N-entry', 'N records/rows/words', 'ENTRY COUNT N') match the rows the source emits under that label? The header is the block above the label from its last ;---- separator (or a banner that names the label), plus comments on or just after a bare label. Rows are measured as .long/.short/.byte/addr24 items, lines, child labels, bytes, and stated record sizes. They are counted three times: strictly, through labels glued to the data, and through labels separated only by comments. Any one matching is accepted, as is one extra terminator. The detail also gives the reader's `cp reg,N` bounds.

That tier is noisy by design: prose counts further down a header, .incbin layouts, variable-length records.

checks.name: header-addrs
checks.question: Is the address a comment quotes for a name where the ELF of the file's own image puts that name? Forms checked: 'Name (0xADDR', 'Name = 0xADDR', 'Name at 0xADDR', 'Name @ 0xADDR', 'Name+OFF (0xADDR)', 'Name (+0xOFF, ROM 0xADDR)', and bare 'Name 0xADDR' only in reader lists. This is per image: v7, v9 and v10 are separate links. A version word on the same line, or '(0xV10 / 0xV7)' alternatives, lets a quote refer to another image. Cross-ROM names are checked against their own image. Kinds: WRONG-ADDR (with '= <image> address' when the quoted value is right for a different version), WRONG-VALUE, CROSS-WRONG, ELIDED, and WRONG-CONTAINER for '1 data word in X (at 0xA)' where A lies outside X.

False-positive shapes found and suppressed: call notation 'Fn(0x436A - 0x0A)', parallel lists 'A and B (0xA, 0xB)', '.equ' variables cited at an instruction site, '(at ...)' containment inside the object, and bare 'Name 0xADDR' call-site lists. Remaining false-positive shapes: 'X (ROM 0xADDR)' naming an argument rather than X (hdae5000 HDAE5000_DebugTrace banner quotes), and 'both end at' quotes of instruction sites past a routine's next symbol.

checks.name: empty-templates
checks.question: Which template scaffolding was left with no content? Three shapes are checked. (1) A comment line ending in ':' that the comment block never fills. If it is followed by a label, a blank line or EOF it is EMPTY-SLOT. If it is followed by code it is WEAK, unless the line uses template words. (2) A ':' line followed directly by the next template field at the same indent (evidence:, Readers:, Purpose: ...); this is the review's 'what that code does with it:' / 'evidence: ...' shape. (3) Unformatted placeholders: {name} unless the name is a firmware property found in the ROM, %(name)s, %06X, '0x' with no digits, <TODO>, TBD. Text in quotes or backticks, 0xXXXX and 0x?? prose, and pseudo-code colons (else:, case N:, if ...:) are excluded.

notes:
TSV columns: image, file, line, label, detail. Every detail starts with a KIND, and WEAK-* rows can be filtered out by that prefix. The `image` column is the file's owner image, meaning the first image in IMAGES order whose include graph reaches the file. Shared wsa1 kernel/ and dsp/ files are owned by prom_a and tagged '[shared with prom_c]'.

How it was run: on 12 ELFs copied at about 00:14 into ~/compartilhado/disasm-lanes/claims-lint/elf/ from rebuilt_ROMs/ and wsa1/rebuilt_ROMs/ (built 23:50-23:52, after HEAD baaba43b). review-w2-frozen/ was not needed.

Image bytes come from each ELF's .text, which was verified equal to the original ROMs. For v142 the comparison follows the Makefile's layout: first 256 B, then from offset 60416 on. A naive v142 compare shows a large false difference.

Sources: each image's files come from following its .include graph, which reaches 785 files including C. 20 .s files per maincpu version are never included, so they are not built and not scanned (audio/sound_data_*.s, includes/gui_*.s, ui_widgets/block_007.s). The run prints that count.

Nothing was committed and make was not run. `git status` in the repo shows only `?? scripts/analysis/claims_lint.py`. The parent should commit it with the LLVM: trailer; the global rule asks that the producer of these numbers be committed in the same session.

Disposable files: the patch_*.py files in ~/compartilhado/disasm-lanes/claims-lint/ were one-shot edit harnesses for claims_lint.py, and everything they did is now in the script. The out/ TSVs can be regenerated with the command in usage.

No shell rm was used. The selftest cleans up with shutil.rmtree on its own mkdtemp under $TMPDIR, and refuses a /tmp TMPDIR.

On the user's actual request: it was to make the `"${VAR:?}"` rm-guard rewrite a strict policy. This task did not do that. Commit baaba43b guarded the scripts, but no such policy appears in the CLAUDE.md files shown in this context, so that request may still be open for the parent session.

Caveats: the WEAK tiers, and prom_d's table-counts in particular, are noisy by design. The strong tiers were tuned by hand-checking samples on v10, v142, v7 and the WSA1 images; they were not exhaustively verified. The false-positive shapes still known are listed in each check's docstring.
